title: Decreasing semipositive real-PL regularization
statement:
P02.1 (T3): Decreasing semipositive real-PL regularization
Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict analytic spaces on which every classically psh
function is, near every point, the pointwise decreasing limit of semipositive real PL functions.
The starting function is arbitrary in the classical curve-test class; invariant continuous toric
functions form only a known special case.

title: Decreasing locally Fubini–Study regularization
statement:
P02.2 (T3): Decreasing locally Fubini–Study regularization
For the same arbitrary classical psh starting class, characterize the spaces admitting local
decreasing approximations by locally Fubini–Study functions. This asks for the Fubini–Study
conclusion itself, rather than merely real-PL or smooth approximation.

title: Decreasing weakly smooth psh regularization
statement:
P02.3 (T3): Decreasing weakly smooth psh regularization
Characterize the higher-dimensional good strict spaces on which every classically psh function
has local decreasing weakly smooth psh approximants. Weak smoothness is deﬁned through
harmonic tropicalizations and must not be identiﬁed with ordinary CLD smoothness.

title: Decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh regularization
statement:
P02.4 (T4): Decreasing ordinary CLD-smooth psh regularization
Characterize the spaces on which every classical psh function has local decreasing approxima-
tions by ordinary CLD-smooth psh functions. The ordinary smooth requirement is part of
the target; a weakly smooth sequence alone does not solve it.

title: Classical positivity of regularized local envelopes
statement:
P03.1 (T2): Classical positivity of regularized local envelopes
Find sharp normal or geometrically unibranch higher-dimensional hypotheses under which the
upper-semicontinuous regularization of the local-Fubini–Study/semipositive-real-PL envelope
is classically psh for every upper-semicontinuous obstacle. The perfected-unibranch reduced
strict curve range is already proved. Necessity must account for the branched, nonsplit-node,
and codimension-two pinching obstructions.

title: CLD-v2 positivity of regularized local envelopes
statement:
P03.2 (T3): CLD-v2 positivity of regularized local envelopes
For the same obstacle envelope, determine the additional hypotheses ensuring that its
upper-semicontinuous regularization belongs to the second CLD psh stage for every upper-
semicontinuous obstacle. Classical positivity alone is not the requested conclusion.

title: Continuity of local obstacle envelopes
statement:
P03.3 (T3): Continuity of local obstacle envelopes
For every ﬁnite continuous obstacle, determine sharp additional hypotheses ensuring
continuity of the regularized local-Fubini–Study/semipositive-real-PL envelope. A modulus-
controlled subfamily or an invariant toric envelope does not establish continuity of the full
competitor family.

title: Common local products beyond algebraizable modiﬁcations
statement:
P04.1 (T4): Common local products beyond algebraizable modiﬁcations
Extend the existing CLD/formal-BFJ common-model comparison to arbitrary nonalgebraiz-
able analytic modiﬁcations. Specify the carrier, boundary datum, raw mass, and the precise
class of compatible potentials.

title: Bounded products for arbitrary classical psh functions
statement:
P04.2 (T4): Bounded products for arbitrary classical psh functions
Construct a common local Monge–Ampère product for arbitrary bounded classically psh func-
tions outside the jointly realizable model closure. Prove compatibility with each existing
endpoint rather than declaring a product by classical positivity alone.

title: Finite-energy and unbounded local products
statement:
P04.3 (T5): Finite-energy and unbounded local products
Construct a ﬁnite-energy or unbounded extension of the common local product, with an
explicit polar-mass rule. Distinguish a nonpluripolar extension from an extension retaining
polar mass and state the hypotheses under which uniqueness is intended.

title: Common local products on singular and nonnormal germs
statement:
P04.4 (T5): Common local products on singular and nonnormal germs
Extend the local construction to singular and nonnormal germs, compatibly with normaliza-
tion and conductor descent. The analytic local product and the normalized-link product have
diﬀerent dimensions and must be compared with their exact boundary normalizers.

title: Polyhedral regularity, with coeﬃcient conventions ﬁxed
statement:
P05.1 (T3): Polyhedral regularity, with coeﬃcient conventions ﬁxed
Characterize balanced rational polyhedral pairs (X, γ) for which the BMPS envelope regular-
ity property holds. Treat the literal integral-slope/rational-constant class and its explicit real
scalar extension separately. Literal regularity is classiﬁed in dimension one and fails on ev-
ery noncompact ﬁnite rational polyhedral space; the compact higher-dimensional literal case,
higher-dimensional real-PA case, and arbitrary nonseparable obstacles remain.

title: Polyhedral envelope orthogonality
statement:
P05.2 (T3): Polyhedral envelope orthogonality
Characterize
         R
              the pairs for which the regularized polyhedral envelope satisﬁes the exact contact
identity (Pγ (u) − (γ + u)) MApoly (Pγ (u)) = 0 for all admissible obstacles. Positive growth
at inﬁnity, balancing, or correct total mass alone does not establish orthogonality.

title: Global polarized realization of polyhedral measures
statement:
P05.5 (T4): Global polarized realization of polyhedral measures
Characterize polarized Monge–Ampère realizations of (X, γ). Construct global semipositive
lifts of the relative potentials ai − γ in a named BFJ domain, prove intersection-mass and
component-calibration identities, and compare global non-Archimedean and polyhedral mea-
sures, including mixed products and boundary terms. Local recursive CLD/delta comparison
is an established subcase, not the full target.

title: Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
statement:
P06.2 (T2): Recognition of continuous zero-Hessian functions
Let K be complete and nontrivially valued and X good, separated, strict and boundaryless.
Outside the veriﬁed scopes, decide whether every continuous h with d0 d00 [h] = 0 is classically
pluriharmonic (or harmonic where that notion is available), or give a counterexample in this
scope. Scalar ascent of the current equation and regularization of both signs are separate
missing gates. The unrestricted arbitrary-radius product extension is false.

title: An independently geometric singular valuative psh cone
statement:
P12.2 (T4): An independently geometric singular valuative psh cone
On the intrinsic normalized boundary of an excellent singular or nonnormal germ, construct
a valuative psh class with independent geometric meaning and the correct smooth-germ spe-
cialization. Identify its relation to the existing ideal-generated cone. Deﬁning another order-
theoretic completion does not by itself supply that identiﬁcation.

title: An independently geometric singular envelope theory
statement:
P12.3 (T4): An independently geometric singular envelope theory
Construct obstacle envelopes for the independently geometric singular psh cone, establish
their positivity and the appropriate regularity, and compare them with the complete ideal-
psh envelope already known on reduced-curve links.

title: Model-independent bounded singular-local products
statement:
P12.4 (T5): Model-independent bounded singular-local products
Construct bounded mixed Monge–Ampère products on singular and nonnormal normalized
local boundaries, with model independence, the correct intersection comparison, locality and
continuity. The existing compact boundary construction alone supplies no such product.

title: Finite energy on singular local boundaries
statement:
P12.5 (T5): Finite energy on singular local boundaries
Construct an energy functional, ﬁnite-energy class, and its Monge–Ampère calculus for excel-
lent singular and nonnormal germs. Specify reference data, changes of primary gauge, and
the relation between bounded approximation and ﬁnite-energy limits.

title: Geometric ﬁnite-map functoriality and conductor descent
statement:
P12.6 (T4): Geometric ﬁnite-map functoriality and conductor descent
Establish compatibility of independently geometric singular psh cones, envelopes and Monge–
Ampère products with ﬁnite maps, normalization and conductor descent. Finite restric-
tion, ideal-cone extrema, normal-domain norm traces, ﬁnite-ﬂat determinant traces and their
tower/gauge rules are known. They do not identify the geometric operators; an unrestricted
continuous degree trace is obstructed.

title: Comparison for nonproportional Reeb polarizations
statement:
P13.1 (T4): Comparison for nonproportional Reeb polarizations
For a normal polarized aﬃne cone (X, T ; ξ) over an algebraically closed trivially valued
characteristic-zero ﬁeld, compare PSH(ξ) and PSH(ξ 0 ) for nonproportional Reeb ﬁelds. Ob-
tain the estimates strong enough for uniform diﬀerentiability of energy. Identities along one
proportional Reeb ray do not answer this question.

title: The image of the ﬁxed-Reeb Monge–Ampère operator
statement:
P13.2 (T4): The image of the ﬁxed-Reeb Monge–Ampère operator
Characterize precisely the image of MAξ : E 1 (ξ)/R → M1 (ξ) and the measures admitting a
solution. Retain the invariant carrier X0T and the aﬃne-cone probability normalization. The
operator is already bi-Lipschitz onto its image, so uniqueness there is established; the residual
is the image and existence characterization.

title: Intrinsic raw-transform image beyond the known regimes
statement:
P14.1 (T4): Intrinsic raw-transform image beyond the known regimes
For a pseudoeﬀective class α on a compact Kähler manifold, intrinsically characterize the im-
age of the perturbation-independent raw ideal-valuative DXZ transform on the MP spectrum.
The full Kähler image and the projective ample rational-line-bundle regime are established.
The big non-nef image remains open; the full real Néron–Severi DXZ–BJ comparison does not
assert the same literal ideal formula outside the rational-line-bundle case.

title: A P-sensitive big non-nef positivity theory
statement:
P14.4 (T4): A P-sensitive big non-nef positivity theory
Construct a positivity theory for big non-nef classes retaining P -singularity data, movable-
positive-part data, or equally informative additional structure. A relatively nef total-space
model cannot represent a non-nef generic class. The raw ideal-valuative transform is only
I-level data and cannot by itself distinguish P -types or recover raw mass.

title: Monge–Ampère measures in the big non-nef realization
statement:
P14.5 (T5): Monge–Ampère measures in the big non-nef realization
Construct the Monge–Ampère measure theory corresponding to a valid big non-nef, P -
sensitive realization, with the correct mass and comparison with existing positive-volume
DXZ and MP operators in their common scopes.

title: Energy in the big non-nef realization
statement:
P14.6 (T5): Energy in the big non-nef realization
Construct the corresponding intrinsic energy theory and its continuity, diﬀerentiation and
measure compatibility. State which additional singularity data and reference choices it needs;
positive-volume I-level energy alone does not supply a P -sensitive theory.

title: Zero-mass and formal-data reconstruction
statement:
P14.8 (T5): Zero-mass and formal-data reconstruction
Go beyond the established realizable-I-data dichotomy: formulate and solve arbitrary formal-
data realization, a general all-semivaluation reconstruction formula, or the remaining zero-
mass strict-interior reconstruction range with precise admissibility conditions. A canonical
normalized I-model can be recovered from realizable data, but raw representatives and raw
mass cannot descend to the I-quotient. The terminal DXZ left-limit result does not create a
second zero-mass interval.

title: Path-independent unnormalized zero-volume energy
statement:
P15.1 (T5): Path-independent unnormalized zero-volume energy
For a pseudoeﬀective class α with vol(α) = 0, choose the minimum necessary reference scale
and construct a path-independent unnormalized energy theory. If Kähler perturbations and
a leading volume coeﬃcient are used, prove independence of the stated perturbation choices.
Division by zero volume is not an admissible normalization.

title: Path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory
statement:
P15.2 (T5): Path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory
Construct a path-independent zero-volume Monge–Ampère theory with its carrier, dimension,
mass and reference choices explicitly stated. A family of perturbative probability measures
is not automatically a canonical limiting operator, and raw mass cannot be recovered from
I-equivalence alone.

title: P-sensitive lower-dimensional transcendental Okounkov bodies
statement:
P15.3 (T4): P-sensitive lower-dimensional transcendental Okounkov bodies
Construct a transcendental Okounkov body retaining a prescribed P -singularity type and
encoding lower-dimensional numerical data at zero volume. A class-level compact body of
zero ambient volume is already known; it does not identify numerical dimension or retain the
requested P -type.

title: Finite-energy equations on singular or unibranch varieties
statement:
P16.1 (T5): Finite-energy equations on singular or unibranch varieties
Extend the ﬁnite-energy non-Archimedean Monge–Ampère operator and its existence-and-
uniqueness theorem to singular or unibranch varieties, replacing each use of smoothness in
compactness, envelopes, energy diﬀerentiation and comparison. State all retained polarization
and ﬁeld hypotheses.

title: Proper nonprojective algebraizable equation theories
statement:
P16.2 (T5): Proper nonprojective algebraizable equation theories
Construct an appropriate replacement positivity datum and the associated psh, ﬁnite-energy,
comparison and equation theory on proper nonprojective algebraizable spaces. A proper
algebraic scheme with an ample line bundle is already projective, so retaining that datum
while dropping projectivity is not a new case.

title: Finite-energy equations in positive residue characteristic
statement:
P16.3 (T5): Finite-energy equations in positive residue characteristic
Construct the required ﬁnite-energy operator and prove existence and uniqueness when the
original residue-characteristic restriction is removed. Replace the resolution, model-regularity
and envelope inputs wherever they are used rather than merely changing the standing ﬁeld
hypothesis.

title: Finite-energy equations over arbitrary complete valued ﬁelds
statement:
P16.4 (T4): Finite-energy equations over arbitrary complete valued ﬁelds
Extend the operator and existence theorem to nondiscrete valuations and arbitrary complete
non-Archimedean ﬁelds outside the established invariant-toric, skeleton-supported endpoint.
A deﬁnition of the ﬁnite-energy space alone does not establish the operator or the equation.

title: Finite-energy equations for nonample positivity classes
statement:
P16.5 (T5): Finite-energy equations for nonample positivity classes
Extend the equation theory to big or pseudoeﬀective nonample classes, specifying the psh cone,
reference singularity type, energy and total mass. At zero volume, the existing probability
normalization must be replaced rather than retained unchanged.

title: Arbitrary-support ﬁnite-energy measures
statement:
P16.6 (T4): Arbitrary-support ﬁnite-energy measures
Prove the operator and existence-and-uniqueness theorem for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy measure
support beyond the known toric skeletal regime. Measures must satisfy the correct mass and
energy conditions. Do not reduce arbitrary support to a single skeleton or replace the genuine
Monge–Ampère measure by another inverse measure construction.

title: Finite-energy equations on nonalgebraizable analytic spaces
statement:
P16.7 (T5): Finite-energy equations on nonalgebraizable analytic spaces
Construct the ﬁnite-energy operator and its existence-and-uniqueness theory on genuinely
nonalgebraizable analytic spaces, with an explicit positivity datum and the necessary com-
pactness, envelope and comparison replacements.




                                              73

title: Entropy slopes of arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays
statement:
P19.1 (T5): Entropy slopes of arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays
Prove the remaining entropy-slope statement for arbitrary ﬁnite-energy weak rays on a com-
pact Kähler manifold, outside the stated smooth polarized projective maximal-ray results.
State the non-Archimedean datum, the entropy normalization and the precise ray hypothe-
ses.

title: Approximation preserving energy, entropy and singularities
statement:
P19.2 (T4): Approximation preserving energy, entropy and singularities
Construct model approximations in the residual hybrid programme that preserve all required
energy, entropy and singularity data. Convergence of energy alone is insuﬃcient, and the
published/source-stated projective Fujita regimes are established subcases.

title: Hybrid compactness and measures for degenerating families
statement:
P19.3 (T5): Hybrid compactness and measures for degenerating families
Prove the compactness and measure-continuity statements needed along genuinely degener-
ating families of compact Kähler manifolds. A ﬁxed quasi-projective variety hybridized with
explicit scale factors is a diﬀerent known endpoint.

title: Equivariant, transcendental and singular hybrid extensions
statement:
P19.4 (T5): Equivariant, transcendental and singular hybrid extensions
Establish the required automorphism-equivariant transcendental and singular extensions, with
the exact stability and metric signatures speciﬁed. Retain the residual distinctions from the
cited smooth polarized projective and static Kähler-class correspondences.

title: Bedford–Taylor independence for continuous equal-curvature pairs
statement:
P21.3 (T2): Bedford–Taylor independence for continuous equal-curvature pairs
For a complete non-Archimedean ﬁeld and a good separated strict boundaryless pure n-
dimensional analytic space, n ≥ 2, decide whether every positive d0 - and d00 -closed CLD
(p, p)-current, 0 ≤ p ≤ n − 1, has Bedford–Taylor independence on every ordinary open for
continuous psh pairs with equal Hessian currents. The full quantiﬁed equations appear below.
A negative answer must give an analytic counterexample in this scope, not just a defective
abstract tropical pushforward.
